- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 1–2% to forecast baseline.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 89.06 → 90.35), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing or lagged decay to avoid overcorrection.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak; if true outcome drops sharply after a peak, model should not continue upward trend beyond 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections; add a 1–3 day lagged correction based on 14-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 7-day true values as anchor for forecast baseline.
